{{Short description|Swiss biologist}}
[[File:Theo & Eiben.jpg|thumb|right|'''Theo Wallimann''', a Swiss [[biologist]]]]
'''Theo Wallimann''' (born 13 October 1946 in [[Alpnach]], [[Obwalden]], Switzerland) is a Swiss biologist who was research group leader and Adjunct-Professor at the Institute of Cell Biology [[ETH Zurich]] and later at the Institute of Molecular Health Science https://mhs.biol.ethz.ch/about-us/emeriti-formermembers/wallimann.html at the [[ETH Zurich]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mhs.biol.ethz.ch/about-us/emeriti-formermembers/wallimann.html|title=Prof. Dr. Theo Wallimann|website=mhs.biol.ethz.ch|language=en|access-date=2019-11-18}}</ref> at the Biology Department https://biol.ethz.ch/en/, of the [[ETH Zurich]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ethz.ch/en/utils/mycontact.NzgxMjY=.html|title=ETH Zürich - Theo Wallimann|website=www.bi.id.ethz.ch|access-date=2019-11-18}}</ref> Switzerland.

== Research and career ==
In 1975, Theo Wallimann completed his Ph.D. Dissertation on “M-line-bound Creatine Kinase and Myofibrillar Structure”<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wallimann |first1=T |last2=Schlösser |first2=T |last3=Eppenberger |first3=HM |title=Function of M-line-bound creatine kinase as intramyofibrillar ATP regenerator at the receiving end of the phosphorylcreatine shuttle in muscle |journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry |date=25 April 1984 |volume=259 |issue=8 |pages=5238–46 |doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(17)42981-4 |pmid=6143755 |doi-access=free }}</ref> in the laboratory of Prof. Hans M. Eppenberger at the Institute of Cell Biology at [[ETH Zurich]] with distinction and received the '''ETH prize and medal'''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Wallimann |first1=Theo |title=Creatinkinase-Isoenzyme und Myofibrillen-Struktur |date=1975 |publisher=ETH Zurich |doi=10.3929/ethz-a-000126732 |hdl=20.500.11850/135936 }}</ref>

From 1975 - 1981, Wallimann worked as a post-doctoral research associate with Andrew G. Szent-Györgyi
,<ref>[https://www.sgpweb.org/page-18130 ''Obituary for Andrew Szent-Györgyi, who passed away at 90 on Jan. 27th 2015 in Falmouth, Mass.'']</ref> at the Biology Department of [[Brandeis University]] on the subject of "Myosin-linked calcium regulation of muscle contraction".<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/40091771_Andrew_G_Szent-Györgyi Andrew G Szent-Györgyi Research Gate]</ref> After rejoining the Biology Dept of the [[ETH-Zurich]] in 1981, Wallimann became a Lecturer in 1984 with his [[Habilitation]] on: "Localization and function of M-line-bound creatine kinase: M-band model and Phospho-Creatine Shuttle"<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Wallimann |first1=Theo |title=Localization and function of M-line-bound creatinekinase: M-band model and creatine-phosphate shuttle |date=1983 |doi=10.3929/ethz-a-000370124 }}</ref>). In 1994, Wallimann was awarded the title of Professor and in the next two years he became Head and Deputy Head of the Institute of Cell Biology. Wallimann resigned from his post in June 2008 and is now [[Emeritus]] and member of the ETH Alumni organisation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.alumni.ethz.ch/en/myalumni.html|title=MyAlumni Platform|website=www.alumni.ethz.ch|language=en|access-date=2019-07-17}}</ref>

In 2005, Wallimann was awarded with <u>the '''Alfred-Vogt-Prize''' i</u>n 2005<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Vogt-Stiftung zur Förderung der Augenheilkunde |url=http://www.alfred-vogt-stiftung.ch/preistraeger.php}}</ref> 

and in 2023, 2024 and 2025 he received the <u>Research.com '''Recognition Leader Award for Biology and Biochemistry in Switzerland'''</u>.<ref>[https://research.com/u/theo-wallimann Theo Wallimann auf ''research.com'']</ref>

In 2025, Theo Wallimann has been honored by the '''International Society of Sports Nutrition''' with a “'''Life-time Achievement Award'''”<ref>[https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12281639/] Life-Time Achievement Award </ref> for his research on the «Creatine Kinase System and Creatine», at the Internatl. Congress on «Creatine for Health», held during March 12th-16th 2025 in Munich, Germany: 
https://creatineforhealth.com/creatine-conference-2025/



Wallimann's main areas of interest are:
*The high-resolution atomic structure, molecular physiology and subcellular compartmentation of [[creatine kinase]] (CK) isoenzymes  (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10737943/), (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10595529/) and (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10737943/) and of the Creatine Transporter (CRT), and in general, micro-compartmentation and metabolite channeling by multi-enzyme complexes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fritz-Wolf |first1=Karin |last2=Schnyder |first2=Thomas |last3=Wallimann |first3=Theo |last4=Kabsch |first4=Wolfgang |title=Structure of mitochondrial creatine kinase |journal=Nature |date=May 1996 |volume=381 |issue=6580 |pages=341–345 |doi=10.1038/381341a0 |pmid=8692275 |bibcode=1996Natur.381..341F |s2cid=4254253 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schlattner |first1=Uwe |last2=Forstner |first2=Michael |last3=Eder |first3=Michael |last4=Stachowiak |first4=Olaf |last5=Fritz-Wolf |first5=Karin |last6=Wallimann |first6=Theo |title=Functional aspects of the X-ray structure of mitochondrial creatine kinase: A molecular physiology approach |journal=Molecular and Cellular Biochemistry |date=1 July 1998 |volume=184 |issue=1 |pages=125–140 |doi=10.1023/A:1006851330913 |pmid=9746317 |s2cid=33526958 }}</ref>
*The mechanisms of the cell enhancing and neuro-protective effects of [[creatine supplements|creatine supplementation]] in health (muscle strength, learning and memory) and disease (neuromuscular and neuro-degenerative disorders).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wallimann |first1=Theo |last2=Tokarska-Schlattner |first2=Malgorzata |last3=Schlattner |first3=Uwe |title=The creatine kinase system and pleiotropic effects of creatine |journal=Amino Acids |date=1 May 2011 |volume=40 |issue=5 |pages=1271–1296 |doi=10.1007/s00726-011-0877-3 |pmid=21448658 |pmc=3080659 }}</ref>(see the recent Conference Volume on "Creatine Supplementation for Health and Clinical Diseases" (2022) https://exerciseandsportnutritionlab.com/news/creatine-in-health-book-published/
*The structure and molecular physiology of AMP-activated protein kinase ([[AMP-activated protein kinase|AMPK]]),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Suter |first1=Marianne |last2=Riek |first2=Uwe |last3=Tuerk |first3=Roland |last4=Schlattner |first4=Uwe |last5=Wallimann |first5=Theo |last6=Neumann |first6=Dietbert |title=Dissecting the Role of 5′-AMP for Allosteric Stimulation, Activation, and Deactivation of AMP-activated Protein Kinase |journal=Journal of Biological Chemistry |date=27 October 2006 |volume=281 |issue=43 |pages=32207–32216 |doi=10.1074/jbc.M606357200 |pmid=16943194 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Riek |first1=Uwe |last2=Scholz |first2=Roland |last3=Konarev |first3=Peter |last4=Rufer |first4=Arne |last5=Suter |first5=Marianne |last6=Nazabal |first6=Alexis |last7=Ringler |first7=Philippe |last8=Chami |first8=Mohamed |last9=Müller |first9=Shirley A. |last10=Neumann |first10=Dietbert |last11=Forstner |first11=Michael |last12=Hennig |first12=Michael |last13=Zenobi |first13=Renato |last14=Engel |first14=Andreas |last15=Svergun |first15=Dmitri |last16=Schlattner |first16=Uwe |last17=Wallimann |first17=Theo |title=Structural Properties of AMP-activated Protein Kinase |journal=Journal of Biological Chemistry |date=27 June 2008 |volume=283 |issue=26 |pages=18331–18343 |doi=10.1074/jbc.M708379200 |pmid=18372250 |doi-access=free }}</ref> involved in cellular energy homeostasis and nutritional signalling, which is relevant for [[type-2 diabetes]], [[obesity]], [[metabolic syndrome]] and [[cancer]].(for publications in PubMed see:<ref>{{PubMedAuthorSearch|Wallimann|T}}</ref> and <ref>{{cite web|url=http://publicationslist.org/theo.wallimann| title=Theo Wallimann publication list}}</ref>).
